title: SOC Analyst I
description:
The Opportunity

Responsibilities

  • Drive containment strategy during data loss or breach events.

  • Triage and resolve advanced vector attacks such as botnets and advanced persistent threats (APTs).

description:

Company name

Full-Time

JOINING

Immediate / short notice

About the Role

CREDO is hiring a SOC Analyst L2 with hands-on experience in security operations, threat detection, and incident response.

You will investigate escalated incidents, hunt for threats, improve detection coverage, and mentor L1 analysts while supporting customers across Microsoft security and cloud environments. This is a shift-based role, and rotational shifts may apply.

What You’ll Do

  • Investigate and respond to escalated and complex incidents across endpoint, identity, email, cloud, and network environments.
  • Analyze and correlate alerts from Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender XDR, and related platforms, using KQL to query and pivot across data sources.
  • Determine the scope, root cause, and impact of incidents; identify IOCs; and map attacker activity to the MITRE ATT&CK framework.
  • Lead containment, eradication, and recovery actions, coordinating with customer IT and security teams.
  • Perform proactive threat hunting based on threat intelligence and known attacker techniques.
  • Develop, tune, and test detection rules to improve coverage and reduce false positives.
  • Build and improve SOC playbooks and runbooks, and automate repetitive response tasks using Sentinel automation rules and playbooks (Logic Apps).
  • Prepare incident reports, post-incident reviews, and clear summaries for technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Review the quality of L1 triage, provide guidance and mentorship, and escalate to L3 or incident response leads when required.
  • Track and report SOC metrics such as MTTD and MTTR.

What We’re Looking For

  • 3–4 years of experience in SOC operations, incident response, or security engineering, including time at L1 level or equivalent.
  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft Defender XDR (Endpoint, Identity, Office 365, and Cloud Apps), along with Microsoft 365 and Azure security.
  • Working proficiency in KQL for investigation and threat hunting.
  • Strong understanding of the incident response lifecycle, common attack techniques, and the MITRE ATT&CK framework.
  • Experience analyzing logs, email headers, network activity, and IOCs, including basic phishing and malware analysis.
  • Excellent analytical, communication, and documentation skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple investigations and priorities effectively, and to work in rotational shifts.

Preferred

  • Experience with SOAR and automation, including Azure Logic Apps, PowerShell, or Python scripting.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Entra ID security, Conditional Access, and Microsoft Purview.
  • Certifications such as SC-200, AZ-500, SC-300, Security+, CySA+, or CEH.

How to Apply

Interested candidates can share their updated CV with the CREDO HR team. Immediate and short-notice joiners are preferred.

title: Infosec Engineer
description:
Company Description


Nemetschek India Private Limited is a global organization and with a legacy of over half a century.
It is a public company listed on MDAX and TecDAX (Germany) stock exchanges. The Nemetschek
Group is a forerunner of digital transformation in the AEC/O (Architecture, Engineering,
Construction & Operations) industry and covers the entire life cycle of construction and
infrastructure projects. With intelligent software solutions, we lead our customers into the future
of digitalization. By using our solutions customers can plan, build, manage, and operate buildings
and infrastructure projects.


Job Description


YOUR ROLE: A chance to make the difference.


We’re looking for a SOC Analyst for our permanent night shift in Hyderabad to focus on
high-quality alert triage and first-line incident handling. You’ll work mainly with CrowdStrike
Falcon, Microsoft Sentinel, and related security tools to keep our global environment safe while
most of the company is asleep.
Experience
  • 3–5 years in a SOC / security monitoring role (L1 or L1/L2 mix).
  • Prior experience in a 24/7 or shift-based SOC is a plus.
Shift details
  • Location: Hyderabad.
  • Permanent night shift, working with EMEA/US time zones.
  • Participation in a rotation that may include weekends and holidays.
  • Clear handover required at the end of each shift to the next region/shift.
ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITY: (Night Shift, triage-focused)
  • Monitor and triage security alerts from EDR/XDR (primarily CrowdStrike Falcon), SIEM
(Microsoft Sentinel), and other security tools.
  • Perform alert-driven incident handling at L1/L1.5 level:
o Quickly review new detections,
o Decide whether to close as benign/false positive, investigate further, or escalate,
o Apply standard playbook-based response actions where allowed (e.g. isolate
host, block hash/domain, disable account with approval).
  • For CrowdStrike Falcon in particular:
o Review detections, examine process trees and related activity,
o Validate severity and impact based on context,
o Close noise/false positives with clear justification or escalate meaningful events.
  • Use Microsoft Sentinel and other platforms to pull additional context during triage (host
history, user activity, geo/access patterns, related alerts).
  • Analyze and respond to phishing alerts and user-reported suspicious emails using
defined playbooks (header analysis, URL/file sandboxing, user follow-up, ticket
updates).
  • Review vulnerability scan results (e.g. Tenable) for basic risk context, confirm exposure
where needed, and follow up with the relevant teams according to priority and SLAs.
  • Conduct basic, playbook-driven “mini threat hunting” during quieter periods (e.g.
running saved queries/hunts in Sentinel and EDR to look for common attacker
techniques or newly published IOCs).
Keep tickets, incident records, and runbooks up to date with short, precise, and complete
investigation notes (what triggered, what you checked, what you decided, and why).
  • Produce clear shift-end handover notes for open incidents and important observations.
WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR:
Core SOC / triage skills
  • 3–5 years of hands-on SOC experience in monitoring, triage, and first-line incident
handling (L1 or L1/L2).
  • Strong focus on alert triage rather than deep forensics: able to work through a queue
efficiently, recognize patterns, and make clear decisions (close, investigate further,
escalate).
  • Experience with:
o At least one enterprise EDR/XDR platform (ideally CrowdStrike Falcon) for alert
analysis and basic response (host isolation, hash/domain blocking, evidence
collection).
o A SIEM platform (ideally Microsoft Sentinel) for correlating alerts and running
queries to gather additional context.
  • Good understanding of security fundamentals:
o Logs: endpoint, authentication, OS, and basic application logs.
o Endpoints: Windows and/or Linux basics, common processes and admin tools.
o Networks: TCP/IP basics, DNS, web traffic, VPN and remote access patterns.
o Common attack techniques across the kill chain (phishing, credential theft,
lateral movement, malware execution, C2, data exfiltration).
Tools and platforms
  • Familiarity with some of the following (or similar solutions):
o CrowdStrike Falcon or another modern EDR/XDR platform.
o Microsoft Sentinel or another SIEM (including experience running and
understanding queries; KQL is a plus).
o Vulnerability management tools such as Tenable.
o Email security / anti-phishing tools, sandboxing, or secure email gateways.
Ways of working and soft skills
Comfortable working permanently in night shift and collaborating with global teams
spread across regions.
  • Strong written communication: able to document alerts, investigations, and handovers in
clear, concise English.
  • Ability to stay calm, structured, and pragmatic during active incidents and high-alert
periods.
  • Habit of following runbooks and escalation paths, while also giving feedback when you
see gaps or improvement opportunities.
  • Ownership mindset: you close the loop on alerts you touch, or you hand them over with
enough context that the next person can continue smoothly.

Qualifications

About Scholar’sEdge Academy

Scholar’sEdge Academy is a skills-and-internship institute in J. P. Nagar, Bengaluru. Every program pairs 3–5 months of live, mentor-led training with a 2-month internship on real projects. Our promise to students is simple: you’ll leave able to show what you can do, not just with a certificate. We’re early, we’re building fast, and the trainer we hire now will shape how we teach cybersecurity.

The role

You’ll train students to work the way a real Security Operations Centre (SOC) team works: watching alerts, investigating suspicious activity, responding to incidents and writing clear reports. You’ll also teach them to secure cloud accounts, where most company data now lives. Everything is taught through hands-on labs, with AI tools used the way security teams use them today: to speed up investigations, never trusted blindly. You’ll be the face of our cybersecurity course, in the classroom, in demo classes and in short videos on our social pages.

What you’ll do

Teach

  • Deliver live, hands-on classes (3 hours a day) covering networking, operating systems, security fundamentals, SOC operations, incident response and cloud security. Spend most of the time in labs, not on slides.
  • Run Saturday labs, free weekend workshops and free demo classes for prospective students and parents.
  • Teach beginners from zero, including non-CS graduates and IT support staff moving into security.

Build proof with students

  • Guide every student through 4–6 lab projects and a capstone. Examples: a home SOC lab with a SIEM, a phishing investigation, brute-force detection from logs, an incident report, and an AWS or Azure security audit.
  • Make sure every student leaves with a GitHub portfolio of lab write-ups and a TryHackMe or similar profile showing completed rooms.
  • Review work every week. Give written feedback, require fixes and track each student’s progress.
  • Mentor students during the 2-month internship: plan real project work, run daily stand-ups and sign off the deliverables.

Keep the course current

  • Help update the syllabus, labs, assignments and quizzes as new threats and tools appear.
  • Run mock interviews for SOC Analyst (L1) roles, and help students prepare for entry-level certifications.

Be the face of the course

  • Appear on camera in 1–2 short teaching videos a week. Scripts and editing support are provided. Examples: “Spot the phishing mail in 30 seconds” or “What a SOC analyst sees on screen.”
  • Answer course questions honestly, and never promise jobs or salaries.
  • Teach ethics first: security skills are used only on systems you own or have written permission to test.

What you must know

Networking

  • Must have: OSI and TCP/IP models, IP addressing and subnetting, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, common ports and protocols, firewalls, VPNs
  • Good to have: packet analysis in depth, network segmentation design

Operating systems

  • Must have: Linux command line, Windows basics, Windows event logs, Active Directory concepts
  • Good to have: Sysmon, Linux log analysis (auth.log, syslog)

Security fundamentals

  • Must have: the CIA triad, common attacks (phishing, malware, ransomware, brute force, SQL injection, XSS), OWASP Top 10, encryption and hashing basics
  • Good to have: vulnerability scanning (Nessus, OpenVAS), Burp Suite basics

SOC operations

  • Must have: what a SIEM does, alert triage, log analysis, the incident response lifecycle, writing incident reports, hands-on with at least one SIEM in a lab (Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Wazuh or Elastic)
  • Good to have: EDR tools (Microsoft Defender, CrowdStrike), threat hunting, SOAR automation, digital forensics basics

Threat intelligence and frameworks

  • Must have: MITRE ATT&CK and the cyber kill chain at a working level, Wireshark, Nmap, VirusTotal and other threat-intelligence sites
  • Good to have: writing detection rules (Sigma, KQL or SPL)

Cloud security

  • Must have: identity and access management (IAM), the shared responsibility model, common cloud misconfigurations, in AWS or Azure
  • Good to have: AWS GuardDuty and Security Hub, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, cloud logging (CloudTrail, Azure Monitor)

AI in security

  • Must have: using AI tools (ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude or similar) to explain logs, write queries and summarise incidents, and teaching students to verify everything they produce
  • Good to have: Microsoft Security Copilot or similar, awareness of AI-specific threats such as prompt injection and deepfake phishing

Scripting and compliance

  • Good to have: Python or PowerShell for automation, ISO 27001 basics, India’s DPDP Act and IT Act basics

Who we’re looking for

  • Freshers, or minimum 1 year of experience in a SOC, security, network or IT support role. Internships count.
  • Freshers must show hands-on proof: a home lab, TryHackMe or Hack The Box progress, CTF results, lab write-ups on GitHub or a blog, or a security certification.
  • Has taught or mentored others, as a trainer, tutor, teaching assistant or college security club lead. Not required, but a strong plus.

  • Strong ethics: teaches only legal, permission-based testing.

  • Degree in CS, IT, electronics or a related field (B.E., B.Tech, BCA, MCA, B.Sc.), or equivalent proven skill. Certifications such as CompTIA Security+, CEH, ISC2 CC, Microsoft SC-200 / SC-900, or AWS / Azure security fundamentals are a plus.

Not a fit: people who only know theory with no labs to show, or who treat hacking as a show-off skill rather than a responsibility.

What we offer

  • Lab and certification support as you teach.
  • A real say in the curriculum of a growing course.
  • Your own visible teaching brand, through on-camera content credited to you.

How to apply

Send your resume, your GitHub, blog or TryHackMe / Hack The Box profile, one lab write-up or incident report and, if you have one, a short teaching video.

Your impact begins here

As SAP Application Security Analyst, you will turn Security Bridge alerts and assessment findings into prioritised, traceable action that protects the SAP landscape behind Novo's finance, supply chain, manufacturing, quality and R&D processes. You will investigate suspicious activity, follow fixes through to verified closure and help redesign S/4HANA roles around least-privilege access. Your work reduces risk in regulated, business-critical systems, so colleagues can keep delivering progress for people living with serious chronic diseases.


What you’ll bring

You are a hands-on SAP security professional who can explain a risk, fix it and prove it is closed. You bring:

  • A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Security or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Five or more years of SAP security, Basis security or SAP cybersecurity experience, including hands-on investigation and remediation.
  • Hands-on PFCG role design, build, troubleshooting and controlled deployment in SAP S/4HANA or ECC, with strong knowledge of authorization objects, organizational levels, and single, composite and master-derived roles.
  • Practical experience with Security Bridge dashboards, threat alerts, vulnerability findings and patch recommendations.
  • Experience with SU24, SU53, STAUTHTRACE, SUIM and AGR_1251 analysis, plus working knowledge of Fiori launchpad content and backend authorizations.
  • A sound understanding of S/4HANA and ECC architecture, RFC connections, SAP Gateway/Fiori and HANA security fundamentals.
  • Experience reviewing SAP security logs and privileged or technical-account activity, and working knowledge of SAP Security Notes, hardening and transports across development, QA and production.
  • Clear written and spoken English, structured analytical skills and the ability to explain technical risks to technical and business audiences.

Useful, but not essential:

  • Security Bridge configuration, detection-content tuning or SIEM/ITSM integration.
  • SAP GRC Access Control or similar tooling, and segregation of duties analysis.
  • Experience in regulated or pharmaceutical environments, including SOX/ITGC controls and GxP change control.
  • Rollout of redesigned roles across business units or countries, including cutover and hypercare; SAP BTP and integration security; relevant SAP or cybersecurity certifications.

What you’ll do

You will work as a hands-on individual contributor, within agreed security standards, access permissions and change-management processes.

  • Monitor and investigate: triage SecurityBridge alerts, separate suspicious activity from expected business or administrative actions, and correlate findings with SAP and HANA logs. Escalate suspected incidents to the SOC and SAP owners within agreed timelines.
  • Prioritise and remediate: validate vulnerabilities against your installed components and business usage, prioritise by severity, exposure and criticality, and drive remediation tickets with clear owners and due dates.
  • Verify closure: rescan or retest after changes, attach evidence and document compensating controls and residual risk where immediate correction is not feasible.
  • Support S/4HANA role redesign: join workshops with functional teams and key users, prepare role-design workbooks, and assess proposed access against least privilege and segregation of duties.
  • Build and maintain approved PFCG roles, Fiori catalogue, space and page assignments and related authorizations, moving changes in a controlled way through development, QA and production.
  • Keep SecurityBridge sharp and auditable: check system coverage and data freshness, tune alerts with documented approval, support SIEM and ITSM integration, and report on response times and finding age in line with SOX/ITGC and GxP procedures.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the SAP Security & Authorizations team in Enterprise IT & Quality, where colleagues work across the Novo value chain to deliver trusted technology, high quality and responsible ways of working. The team supports security architecture, access governance and operational security across a global SAP landscape serving business-critical and GxP-regulated processes.

Your closest partner is the SAP Security Architect, who you will agree priorities with and escalate design changes and unresolved risk to. You will also work with Basis, HANA database administrators, ABAP developers, business application teams, cybersecurity/SOC, functional teams, key users and external service providers. Clear ownership and open, timely communication keep findings and role changes moving, so risk is reduced faster.


What you can expect here

You will be trusted to own your work, with clear expectations and the support to perform at your best. You will build new skills across SAP security, access governance and monitoring, and see your contribution in measurable risk reduction across a global landscape. Your voice counts: you will be encouraged to share your expertise and challenge how things are done, then commit and move forward together.


Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn security findings into verified progress across a global SAP landscape, apply for the SAP Application Security Analyst role by 25 November 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Work Mode: Hybrid (3 days)

Application Deadline- 25 November 2026

  • Ability to integrate agentic pipelines with enterprise systems via MCP or REST/event APIs
  • Capability to reverse-engineer requirements and domain models from legacy or unfamiliar codebases using AI-assisted analysis and translate them faithfully into a new target stack
  • Practical context management skills, including prompt/context window structuring, retrieval and chunking strategies, and multi-step agent memory management
  • Experience implementing AI guardrails such as input/output validation, PII redaction, hallucination and scope-of-action checks, and human-in-the-loop approval gates
  • Working knowledge of tokenomics, including token usage/cost estimation, model selection trade-offs, and designing agent workflows within latency/cost budgets
  • AI/LLM security awareness, including prompt-injection defense, secure handling of secrets/credentials, and least-privilege scoping for agent actions

threat intelligence analysis. The role will lead initiatives to identify emerging cyber threats, develop and optimize security detection mechanisms, and improve visibility across the organization's IT infrastructure, applications,and cloud environments.



The individual will leverage internal security telemetry, external threat intelligence feeds, and industry threat-sharing communities to identify potential attack patterns, develop actionable detection strategies,

and proactively uncover adversarial activities that may bypass conventional security controls.




The role requires prior hands-on experience as a SOC Analyst, along with strong expertise in threat detection, security monitoring, incident investigation, and threat hunting.



Key Responsibilities



Detection Engineering

  • Design, develop, implement, and continuously fine-tune custom threat detection rules and use cases.
  • Map detection capabilities and security monitoring coverage against the MITRE ATT&CK framework.
  • Identify detection gaps across endpoints, networks, applications, cloud platforms, and enterprise environments.
  • Develop and optimize SIEM detection rules,correlation logic, behavioral analytics, and automated alerts.
  • Collaborate with SOC and incident response teams to improve detection accuracy and minimize false positives.
  • Develop and enhance threat detection use cases to identify unauthorized access, suspicious activity, data exfiltration, and potential compromise involving sensitive healthcare information and patient data.
  • Design and optimize security monitoring mechanisms to detect anomalous access patterns, potential data breaches, and threats targeting systems that store, process, or transmit Electronic Protected Health Information (ePHI).


Threat Intelligence Management

  • Collect, analyze, and operationalize threat intelligence from internal security telemetry, commercial intelligence feeds, open-source intelligence (OSINT), and Information Sharing and Analysis Centers (ISACs).
  • Analyze emerging threat actors, attack techniques,indicators of compromise (IOCs), and adversarial tactics.
  • Translate threat intelligence into actionable detection rules, threat-hunting hypotheses, and security priorities.
  • Maintain awareness of evolving cyber threats,vulnerabilities, attack campaigns, and industry-specific risks.
  • Establish processes for integrating threat intelligence into security monitoring and incident response operations.


Proactive Threat Hunting

  • Lead proactive threat-hunting activities to identify suspicious behavior and advanced adversarial activities that may bypass automated security tools.
  • Develop threat-hunting hypotheses based on intelligence reports, MITRE ATT&CK techniques, and observed security events.
  • Investigate abnormal activities across endpoint, network, identity, application, and cloud environments.
  • Perform advanced log analysis, event correlation, and behavioral analysis to uncover hidden threats.
  • Document hunting findings and translate identified threats into improved detection mechanisms and security controls.


SOC Operations & Incident Investigation

Leadership & Continuous Improvement

  • Collaborate with infrastructure, cloud, application security, and security operations teams to strengthen the organization's overall security posture.
